summary: Digit-string formatter used by CRT-style number-to-string conversion. Writes a leading '0' (48) at a1[0], copies a2 digit characters from the stream at a3+12 into the buffer (substituting '0' for a zero byte), NUL-terminates the result, applies round-up with carry propagation when the next unconsumed digit is 5 or greater, then skips a leading '0' via sub_58B130 when the leading digit did not round up; on carry overflow into the leading digit it increments the counter at a3+4.

operations.description: Initialize the first buffer byte a1[0] to '0' (48) and start the result pointer at a1+1.
Load the digit source pointer from a3+12 and initialize the second output byte position (a1+1).
Guard on a2 > 0 to decide whether the digit-copy loop runs at all.
Loop a2 times copying each byte from the source stream into the buffer; a zero byte in the stream is substituted with '0' (48).
NUL-terminate the formatted string at the final result position.
Guard combining the consumed-count sign (v4 >= 0) with the next unconsumed digit being >= '5' (53) to trigger rounding.
Round-up carry propagation: walk back replacing '9' (57) digits with '0' (48) until a non-9 digit is found, then increment it.
Guard on a1[0] == '1' (49) after rounding, indicating the carry overflowed into the leading digit.
On leading-carry, increment the counter at a3+4 and return the pointer past the leading digit.
Otherwise measure the digit-string length with Strlen and shift the buffer left by one byte via sub_58B130, discarding the leading '0'.
Return the shifted buffer pointer produced by sub_58B130 in the leading-zero-skip path.
